name: frontend-design
purpose: Guide distinctive, usable, and verifiable DataSwarm interface design for chat, artifacts, trace, skills, projects, settings, and swarm execution views.
activationGuidance: Use when the user asks to design, redesign, critique, polish, or diagnose frontend UI, UX, layout, typography, visual style, interaction states, or product copy.
Use when changing DataSwarm conversation flow, artifact preview, trace pages, skills/projects/settings management, swarm branch visualization, or runtime cards.
Use before implementing broad UI changes so the planner can establish a concrete design direction, quality bar, and verification checklist.
Do not use for backend-only runtime, database, sandbox, or tool adapter work unless the change affects what users see or control.

finalAnswerRequirements: state the concrete surface being designed
explain the design direction and the tradeoffs
include responsive, overflow, accessibility, and interaction-state verification
separate confirmed UI defects from aesthetic recommendations when diagnosing an existing screen

qualityChecks: design decisions are specific to DataSwarm's agentic workspace rather than generic SaaS styling
layout preserves stable conversation flow, fixed navigation, bounded artifact previews, and readable runtime cards
long titles, ids, hashes, tool payloads, tables, code blocks, and iframes cannot expand outside their containers
states for idle, running, streaming, completed, failed, empty, disabled, hover, focus, and loading are accounted for
keyboard focus, contrast, reduced motion, mobile width, and desktop density are explicitly considered
final UI copy uses user-recognizable product language instead of internal implementation jargon
